planting.note: Plant tubers once soil has warmed in spring; ruffled waterlily blooms appear on strong branching stems through summer.

directions: 'Sandia Rose' is a waterlily-form dahlia with ruffled, medium pink petals arranged in shallow, flat-backed layers around a glowing center, giving each roughly 5-inch bloom the classic open waterlily look. Vigorous, well-branched plants hold flowers on long, strong stems that are excellent for cutting. Grow in full sun with rich, well-drained soil and even moisture, staking in exposed sites, then lift and store tubers after frost blackens the foliage.

planting.note: Part of the Karma series bred for cut-flower production; plant tubers after soil has warmed and expect a long, heavy bloom flush into fall.

directions: 'Karma Amora' is a waterlily-form dahlia in the Dutch-bred Karma series, bearing vermillion-scarlet, double, flat-faced blooms around 6 inches across on tall, rigid stems built for the vase. Developed specifically for cut-flower growers, it offers unusually long vase life and reliable, upright stem strength without staking in most gardens. Plant tubers in full sun after frost danger has passed, keep soil evenly moist, and lift for winter storage in colder climates.

planting.note: A prolific cut-flower waterlily type; plant tubers 4-6 inches deep once the soil has warmed in spring.

directions: 'Silver Years' bears soft blush-pink, double waterlily blooms around 4 inches across with a pale cream center, set against large, dark green serrated foliage for strong contrast. Thin but very strong, dark stems make it a favorite for bouquets and market cutting gardens, with plants branching freely from summer through frost. Grow in full sun with consistent moisture and good air circulation, and lift tubers for storage before hard frost.

planting.note: A compact border peony-type registered in 1990 by J. Robbie and originated at Longwood Gardens, Pennsylvania; plant tubers after frost danger passes and no staking is usually required.

directions: 'Longwood Dainty' is a compact peony-flowered dahlia bearing soft peach to rust-orange blooms around 1.5 inches wide, with two to three loose rows of petals surrounding an open center typical of the peony form. Its low, tidy habit makes it well suited to border edges and containers rather than cutting beds. Grow in full sun with well-drained soil, water regularly through the growing season, and lift tubers for winter storage where the ground freezes.

planting.note: Registered in the Netherlands in 2001 by L. Verhoeven; plant tubers once soil has warmed and expect free branching for a long bloom season.

directions: 'Floorinoor' is an anemone-flowered dahlia with smooth, slightly rounded pink outer ray petals surrounding a dense, textured cushion center in orange, giving each 3-4 inch bloom strong depth and movement. Plants branch freely on upright stems, producing flowers from summer through fall, and the pincushion centers are a magnet for pollinators. Plant in full sun in moist, fertile, well-drained soil, and lift tubers for storage after frost.

planting.note: Introduced by Swan Island Dahlias in 2005 and winner of the ADS Derrill W. Hart Award in 2016; sturdy upright stems generally need no staking.

directions: 'Zippity Do Da' is a true pompon dahlia producing tight, perfectly round, fully double blooms about 2 inches across in candy pink to lilac tones with a deeper raspberry eye, the neatly curved petals giving each flower crisp, ball-like precision. Its strong, upright 3- to 3.5-foot plants need no staking and bloom nonstop from summer to frost, making it a reliable choice for cutting gardens and borders. Grow in full sun with regular water, and lift tubers before winter in climates where the ground freezes.

planting.note: A US-bred orchid-form introduction from Dan's Dahlias' Washington-state breeding program; tall stems benefit from support in open, windy sites.

directions: 'Tahoma Hope' is an orchid-flowered dahlia with a single to double row of long, inward-curving pure white petals around an open center, giving each flower a star-like, airy silhouette distinct from fully double decorative types. Tall, strong stems and prolific, repeat flowering make it a favorite for cutting gardens. Grow in full sun with consistent moisture, stake in exposed locations, and lift tubers for winter storage where the ground freezes.

planting.note: Part of the dark-leaved 'Classic' peony-flowered series; plant tubers once soil has warmed in spring.

directions: 'Classic Rosamunde' is a peony-flowered dahlia with bright pink, semi-double blooms 4-6 inches across that echo a Japanese anemone in form, set off dramatically by deep bronze-black foliage. Highly floriferous from midsummer until frost, it works equally well in borders, containers, and cutting arrangements. Grow in full sun with evenly moist, well-drained soil, and lift and store tubers over winter in climates with freezing ground.
